name: cad
$comment-opencascade: OCCT 8.0.1 (2026-07-30). C++17 minimum. DataExchange toolkits are TKDE*-prefixed since 7.8. VTK deliberately not requested; it is off by default in OCCT 8 anyway. The freetype default feature is kept: dropping it would shed fontconfig/gperf/brotli/libpng, but that is minutes against OCCT's own 30-60, and a USE_FREETYPE=OFF build is unverified — it would fail deep into the OCCT compile, costing a full CI cycle per attempt.

dependencies.name: opencascade
dependencies.$comment: default-features OFF drops opencascade's `freetype` feature, which pulls freetype AND fontconfig. Both are hosted on gitlab.freedesktop.org, which serves 504s reliably enough from the GitHub arm64 runners that the Linux arm64 job could never finish a cold build -- three separate runs, three different packages from that one host. We never use OCCT's text rendering: nothing links TKV3d or TKService, and the renderer is bgfx. USE_FREETYPE only feeds OCCT's own visualisation.

shell-libgui.description: The libgui desktop shell (prototype): SDL3 for windows, input, clipboard and file dialogs

$comment-dime: DXF read and write (Coin3D dime), BSD-3-Clause. Chosen over libdxfrw and dxflib specifically because those are GPL-2.0: linking either would raise vCAD floor to GPL and make proprietary plugins impossible. See COPYRIGHT.md. Entity coverage includes Line/Arc/Circle/Ellipse/Spline/LWPolyline/Polyline/Point/Insert, and UnknownEntity round-trips what it does not parse.
$comment-boost: planegcs needs Boost.Graph (connected_components, to partition a sketch into independent subsystems) and Boost.Math (constants). Header-only, so vcpkg copies headers rather than compiling. Requested instead of patching the vendored solver: reimplementing connected_components would be reinventing, and every edit to vendored code makes the next upstream sync a merge.
$comment-sqlite3: The native document format (ADR 0003). Requested explicitly rather than relying on the platform's copy: macOS and most Linux ship libsqlite3, Windows ships nothing, and assetlib's find_package(SQLite3 QUIET) was silently picking up the system one. A single C file -- seconds to build, and it does not touch OCCT.
$comment-bgfx: bgfx 1.129 with [tools] for shaderc. The tools feature pulls glslang and spirv-tools -- a real but one-time build. Compiling shaders from source beats checking in per-platform binary blobs nobody can regenerate. glfw3 was removed on 15 Aug 2026: nothing linked it. The only two mentions left in the tree are comments, one of which records that the hidden GLFW window it existed for had already been deleted. It pulled vcpkg's whole X11/xcb chain from source on Linux, and one of those tarballs (xcb-util-m4, from gitlab.freedesktop.org) served 504s reliably enough to keep the arm64 job from ever completing a cold build.
$comment-nlohmann-json: Tests only: tests/oracle replays SolidCraft's reference-part recipes, which are JSON. Header-only, MIT. In the tests feature so no shipped binary links it; if commands come to take JSON parameters, the app will need a JSON library of its own and that is a separate decision.
$comment-sdl3: SDL3 is the libgui shell's host (windows, input, IME, clipboard, native file dialogs), behind the shell-libgui feature so no other build pulls it. default-features OFF on purpose: SDL3's Linux defaults include ibus, which builds dbus from gitlab.freedesktop.org -- the host whose 504s got glfw3 removed (see $comment-bgfx). x11 and wayland take no vcpkg dependencies; they use the system headers. Linux IME through ibus is to be added deliberately, not by default.
